title: NIH RePORTER (research grants)
questions: NIH funding for Alzheimer's research by year
NIH grants to universities in a state
which institutions get the most NIH money

manual.how: The API takes POST requests, so a browser link cannot fetch them: run download_data.sh / download_data.ps1 from the bundle (one command, no Python), or search at https://reporter.nih.gov/advanced-search (same criteria), click Export, choose CSV and the fields, and upload the file. Whole fiscal years: https://reporter.nih.gov/exporter (bulk CSV files).

cache.why: Searches are small; RePORTER adds awards weekly. data/ is reused within a run.

redistribution.why: RePORTER data describe federal awards and are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Abstracts are written by applicants; quote them sparingly.

citation: National Institutes of Health, RePORTER: {dataset}, api.reporter.nih.gov, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Fiscal year of the award (fiscal_years) or project period? RePORTER rows are project-year awards by federal fiscal year (October-September).
Topic by RCDC spending category (NIH's official categorization) or by text search (broader, noisier)? Official RCDC totals are at report.nih.gov and are not the sum of this search.

NIH only? RePORTER also holds AHRQ, CDC (its centers: NCEH, NIOSH, ...), FDA and VA awards (FY2024: AHRQ 497, FDA 560, VA 2,181 projects); list the NIH institutes in agencies, and check agency_ic_admin, to exclude them.
